page: Microsoft Azure D32plds_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine belonging to the Dpldsv6 server family. It is powered by a Microsoft Neoverse-N2 processor featuring 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.4 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with a 1890 GB NVMe SSD and supports Premium Storage. The architecture lacks hyper-threading, allocating exactly one thread per physical core, and does not include any GPU hardware.

In benchmark evaluations, the D32plds_v6 demonstrates strong multi-core performance, as evidenced by its top 25% ranking in multi-core stress-ng and Geekbench tests. Memory performance is a notable highlight, with large-block read-only memory bandwidth and PassMark memory scores reaching the top 10% tier. Database operations also perform in the top 10% tier under PassMark testing, complemented by strong Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput in the top 25%. However, single-core performance metrics, such as single-core stress-ng and Geekbench scores, remain in the average tier. Large-scale LLM inference presents a performance tradeoff, with prompt processing for 70B models falling into the bottom 10% tier, though text generation for the same model size stabilizes at an average level.

The qualitative cost profile of this instance is defined by its ARM-based architecture and low memory-to-CPU ratio, which offers a resource-dense compute option without the overhead of larger memory allocations. The inclusion of a fast 1890 GB local NVMe SSD provides high-speed local storage directly bundled with the compute resources. Given these characteristics, the D32plds_v6 is well-suited for multi-threaded compute tasks, software compilation, database operations, and static web serving. It is less optimal for memory-intensive applications or large-scale LLM inference workloads.
